
```{python}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
np.random.seed(42)
```


## Correlogramm

Define a function to compute a correlogramm

```{python}
def correlogram(spikes1, spikes2, bin_size=0.001, window=0.05):
    is_auto = np.array_equal(spikes1, spikes2)

    bins = np.arange(-window, window + bin_size, bin_size)
    bin_centers = bins[:-1] + bin_size/2
    counts = np.zeros(len(bins) - 1)

    for i, spike in enumerate(spikes1):

        mask = np.abs(spikes2 - spike) <= window
        if is_auto: # exclude self-reference
            mask[i] = False

        if np.any(mask):
            time_diffs = spikes2[mask] - spike
            hist, _ = np.histogram(time_diffs, bins=bins)
            counts += hist
    
    counts = counts / (len(spikes1))

    return bin_centers, counts
```


Simulate some data to test how CCG works. Let's assume two cases: one where two neurons fire synchronously and one where they fire with a fix delay.

```{python}
t = np.linspace(0, 10, 10000)
spikes1_sync = t[np.random.random(10000) < 0.1]
spikes2_sync = spikes1_sync + np.random.normal(0, 0.002, len(spikes1_sync))
spikes1_delay = t[np.random.random(10000) < 0.1]
spikes2_delay = spikes1_delay + 0.005 + np.random.normal(0, 0.002, len(spikes1_delay))
```

Plot the compute and plot the CCG for both cases

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1,2, sharex=True, sharey=True)
bins, probabilities = correlogram(spikes1_sync, spikes2_sync)
ax[0].bar(bins * 1e3, probabilities, width=1.0, align='center')
bins, probabilities = correlogram(spikes1_delay, spikes2_delay)
ax[1].bar(bins * 1e3, probabilities, width=1, align='center')
ax[0].set(xlabel="Time Lag [ms]", ylabel="Spike Coincidence [a.u.]", title="Synchronous")
ax[1].set(xlabel="Time Lag [ms]", title="Synchronous", xlim=(np.min(bins*1e3), np.max(bins*1e3)))
plt.show()
```

## Autocorrelogram

Simulate two independent neurons with a refractory period of 2s

```{python}
def generate_spikes_with_refractory(duration=10, rate=10, refractory=0.002):
    spikes = []
    t = 0
    while t < duration:
        interval = np.random.exponential(1/rate)
        interval = max(interval, refractory)
        t += interval
        if t < duration:
            spikes.append(t)
    return np.array(spikes)
```

```{python}
spikes1 = generate_spikes_with_refractory(rate=50)
spikes2 = generate_spikes_with_refractory(rate=50)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1,2, sharex=True, sharey=True)
bins, probabilities = correlogram(spikes1, spikes2, bin_size=0.0005, window=0.03)
ax[0].bar(bins * 1e3, probabilities, width=1.0, align='center')
bins, probabilities = correlogram(spikes1, spikes1, bin_size=0.0005, window=0.03)
ax[1].bar(bins * 1e3, probabilities, width=1, align='center')
ax[0].set(xlabel="Time Lag [ms]", ylabel="Spike Coincidence [a.u.]", title="Cross-Correlogram")
ax[1].set(xlabel="Time Lag [ms]", title="Auto-Correlogram", xlim=(np.min(bins*1e3), np.max(bins*1e3)))
plt.show()
```

## Use the Autocorrelogram to indetify Neurons

Read the spike clusters
```{python}
probability_treshold = 0.5
df = pd.read_csv("spike_clusters.csv")
prob_mask = df["Probability"]>probability_treshold
```

Plot all autocorrelogramms to identify (lack of) a refractory period.

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(5,3)
for i_c in range(df["Cluster"].max()+1):
    axis = ax.flatten()[i_c]
    spikes = df[df["Cluster"]==i_c]["Time"].values
    spikes.sort()
    bins, probabilities = correlogram(spikes, spikes, bin_size=0.0005, window=0.02)
    axis.bar(bins * 1e3, probabilities, width=1, align='center')
    axis.set(title=f"Cluster {i_c}", xticks=[], yticks=[])
plt.show()
```

Identify Clusters that could be units

```{python}
unit_clusters = [3,5,8,9]
```

## Visualize the clusters

```{python}
pca_features = np.load("pca_features.npy")
```

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(2,3)
p = 0
labels = ['Ch1','Ch2','Ch3','Ch4']
for i in np.arange(0,4):
    for j in np.arange(i+1,4):
        axis = ax.flatten()[p]
        for c in unit_clusters:
            data = pca_features[df["Cluster"]==c, :, :]
            axis.scatter(data[:,0, i], data[:,0, j], label=c, s=5) 
        axis.set(xlabel=labels[i], ylabel=labels[j], xlim=(-1500,1500), ylim=(-1500, 1500), xticks=[], yticks=[])
        p = p+1
        axis.legend()
plt.show()
```

3, 5 and 8 seem to represent neurons, 9 clearly doesn't.
Let's save them in a new data frame.

```{python}
unit_clusters={3:1, 5:2, 8:3}
df_units = df.copy()[df["Cluster"].isin([3,5,8])]
df_units["Unit"] = 0
for key, value in unit_clusters.items():
    df_units.loc[df_units["Cluster"]==key, "Unit"] = value
df_units.drop(columns=["Cluster", "Probability"])
df.to_csv("units.csv", index=False)
```
